The analysis is a within-group, whole-brain PET task activation examining prospective memory, which involves executive processes (holding an intention and monitoring for targets). The task falls within the six executive domains (notably vigilance/maintenance and working-memory-like retention) and the contrast is a main effect of the task vs baseline, reflecting executive demand.

Although the task requires holding target words, it is not a canonical working-memory paradigm (e.g., n-back, Sternberg) as required by the local inclusion criteria; the contrast isolates prospective memory/target-monitoring rather than a defined working-memory manipulation or load effect.
The task does not involve inhibiting a prepotent response or classic inhibitory paradigms (e.g., Go/No-Go, Stroop); it instead involves maintaining intentions and target detection.
The contrast does not reflect task- or rule-switching demands (no task-switching or set-shifting paradigm is described).
The task is not a planning paradigm (e.g., Tower of London/Hanoi) and does not isolate planning demands.

Prospective memory here requires maintaining a monitoring set and detecting target words during ongoing activity (target-detection/tapping when repeating targets), matching vigilance/target-detection paradigms; the contrast is a task main effect reflecting set-maintenance/target detection demand.
The task does not involve verbal or self-initiated generation (word generation/fluency) and therefore does not meet initiation criteria.

This contrast ('viewing words > false fonts', I1; N1 > I4; N4) is a visual/linguistic stimulus contrast rather than a contrast of executive demand. Although global criteria such as GLOBAL_I3 (within-group, whole-brain) are met for this analysis, the local pooled criterion requiring the contrast to reflect executive demand is not met (missing POOLED_EXECUTIVE_FUNCTION_I2). Also the contrast does not reflect an executive-task-specific manipulation (GLOBAL_I8 not satisfied for this contrast).

The task is a Stroop paradigm but this specific contrast compares words to false fonts (visual/language processing) and does not reflect working-memory load or maintenance. Local exclusion WORKING_MEMORY_E1 applies.

Although the overarching task is Stroop, this particular contrast (viewing words > false fonts) isolates visual/linguistic stimulus processing rather than inhibitory demand (incongruent > congruent or Stroop main effect). Local exclusion INHIBITION_E1 applies.
The contrast does not involve task switching or set-shifting; it contrasts words versus false fonts. Local exclusion COGNITIVE_FLEXIBILITY_E1 applies.
The contrast is not a planning paradigm (Tower tasks); it isolates visual/linguistic processing. Local exclusion PLANNING_E1 applies.
The contrast does not index sustained target-detection or set maintenance (oddball/vigilance); it contrasts words vs false fonts. Local exclusion VIGILANCE_E1 applies.
This contrast does not index self-initiated generation (word generation paradigms); it contrasts viewing words with false fonts. Local exclusion INITIATION_E1 applies.
